In summary, our research is concerned with
the induction of mutation in Oncidium in vitro and the analysis of RAPD of regenerated plantlets.
the effects of EMS on mutation induction of Oncidium in vitro cultured TCLs and the polymorphisms of RAPD of the regenerated plantlets.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mutagen EMS could be used to induce mutations of Oncidium and the concentration 0.4%(0.4 g/L) is suitable for Oncidium chemical induction in the experiment.
mutagen EMS has some injured effects on Oncidium PLBs and the injured effects got more serious with higher concentrations of mutagens and prolonged exposure time.
the concentration of 0.2-0.4% and 2-6h treatment of EMS were suitable for Oncidium PLBs chemical induction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mutagens had obvious effects on PLBs and regenerated plantlets,there were polymorphisms of RAPD and the ratio of RAPDs polymorphisms had some relation to the concentration of mutagens.
the chemical induction in vitro of Oncdium had a good effect, but it was necessary to choose suitable concentration and treatment time.
the mutation of EMS in Oncdium PLB in vitro culture had some injured effects and the concentration of EMS had some influence on the mutation and the RAPD analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of RAPD analysis to study the mutation induction of EMS in vitro cultured Oncidium PLBs was feasible.
EMS can induce mutations of Oncidium and the concentration of 0.1%,0.2% and 0.4 % are suitable for Oncidium in vitro chemical induction.
the mutation of Oncidium in vitro cultured with EMS has been successfully induced and it is possible to get new varieties of Oncidium through the method of in vitro mutation breeding.
